findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the contradiction between 'bounded escalation' (AC4 guarantee) and the fail-open counter: either add a fallback (e.g., cast the -1 immediately when the attempt write fails, forfeiting the retry), or explicitly weaken AC4 to 'bounded when counter storage is healthy' and add a monitoring/alerting requirement for persistent VOTER_ERROR sequences.
evidence: "an uncounted attempt only delays escalation by one cycle" — this claim holds only for a single isolated failure; persistent SQLite write failures mean escalation never fires
AC4 states the Nth failure 'casts the fail-closed -1' as a guarantee, but the fail-open counter makes this conditional on counter storage being healthy
The section header calls this 'a bounded escalation' yet the mechanism has no fallback when the bounding store is unavailable
findings.finding: The 'bounded escalation' guarantee (Change 2 section header, AC4) is contradicted by the fail-open counter strategy: if SQLite writes persistently fail, review_attempts is never incremented and escalation never fires, making the bound effectively infinite — directly contradicting 'bounded escalation'.
findings.location: Change 2 — 'bounded escalation' header and the paragraph: 'a SQLite failure on that write is caught and logged as VOTER_ERROR and the deferral still returns vote-less (an uncounted attempt only delays escalation by one cycle)'
scenarios: SQLite database corruption or permission loss causes every attempt_count write to fail; the change is deferred vote-less indefinitely with no escalation and no human alert beyond a VOTER_ERROR log per cycle
A disk-full condition on the host causes persistent write failures; the change is stuck and never escalates
findings.suggested_fix: In voter.py, when the attempt_count write raises a SQLite exception, cast the fail-closed -1 immediately (treat a counter-write failure as an instant escalation) rather than deferring vote-less. This restores the bounded guarantee: the change gets a vote no matter what state the counter store is in.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that `record_attempt` uses a single atomic SQL statement for the increment (e.g., `INSERT INTO review_attempts ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET attempts = attempts + 1`) rather than a read-modify-write sequence.
evidence: 'INSERT/increment' — ambiguous whether this is a single atomic SQL statement or a read-then-write
SQLite supports atomic `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO ... SELECT COALESCE(...) + 1` or `UPDATE ... SET attempts = attempts + 1` patterns
ABSENCE: no explicit atomicity guarantee stated for the counter increment
findings.finding: The `record_attempt` operation is described as 'INSERT/increment' but the atomicity of this operation is unspecified. A non-atomic read-then-write (SELECT count + INSERT-or-UPDATE) is a TOCTOU race. While the bot likely runs as a single async process, the reconciler also interacts with the DB, and future concurrency (or a test harness running parallel workers) could produce a lost-update on the attempt counter.
findings.location: Change 2 — 'The attempt is recorded (INSERT/increment) BEFORE the deferral return'; Scope `dedup.py`
scenarios: Two coroutines (voter and reconciler-driven re-review) concurrently hit `record_attempt` for the same (change_id, revision); both read count=2, both write count=3; the effective count is 3 instead of 4, delaying escalation by one cycle — minor but violates the stated bounded-retry guarantee
findings.suggested_fix: Use SQLite's `INSERT INTO review_attempts(change_id, revision, attempts) VALUES(?, ?, 1) ON CONFLICT(change_id, revision) DO UPDATE SET attempts = attempts + 1` as the single atomic statement.

findings.finding: The `force=True` path (used by the existing `/rerun` endpoint) is not specified to bypass the new attempt-cap check. When a change has exhausted its retry budget (attempt_count ≥ RETRYABLE_GAP_MAX_ATTEMPTS), a `/rerun` call will read the counter, find it ≥ cap, and immediately re-cast the escalated fail-closed `-1` WITHOUT performing a fresh review — the opposite of the intended recovery behavior. bb9b ships `reset_attempts` as the remedy, but operators relying on the existing `/rerun` before bb9b lands will observe the re-escalation silently.

scenarios: Operator sees a capped `-1` (retries exhausted), triggers `/rerun` (the existing recovery tool), but the voter reads attempt_count=3 ≥ cap=3 and immediately re-casts the escalated `-1` without reviewing — /rerun provides no relief until bb9b's reset API ships

findings.suggested_fix: In the 'voter.review_and_vote' deferral spec, add: 'When force=True, skip the attempt-cap check entirely (do not consult review_attempts); the operator is explicitly requesting a fresh review.' This keeps /rerun functional as a recovery tool independently of bb9b, and bb9b's reset_attempts is still needed for non-forced re-drives.
